hold_text:
R5 named it and the guard is right. This PR now contains `.gitattributes`, which is outside TIER1_SURFACE — not dangerous, but not something the guard can certify, so self-landing is refused rather than granted by default.

The path arrived after this branch declared `landing: "self"`: the manager landed `76512ff8a` here (binding `docs/claude/work/PIPELINE.jsonl` to `merge=union`), taking up the escalation this lane filed as PI-20260922-PHOUDXG4-0001. That is a deliberate, argued change by its author — see the PR comment — so the lane did NOT back it out to keep its own self-land. Narrowing the PR is R5's other remedy and it would mean reverting someone else's considered commit to preserve a convenience for this one; holding is the honest move and it is the one the guard's own remedy text names.

⚠️ THE HOLD IS REAL, NOT DECORATIVE. The `.github/pr-automerge-requests/` marker is removed and GitHub auto-merge is disabled in the same change. Leaving the route armed under a `hold` declaration would land the PR on green with nobody having read it — a hold in name only, which is worse than no hold because it reads as a human gate that does not exist.

WHAT A HUMAN IS BEING ASKED TO READ: one line of `.gitattributes` (plus its measurement comment) binding PIPELINE.jsonl to git's built-in `merge=union`. Its evidence is in the PR body and in the manager's comment — 23/23 conflicts → 0/23, the union objection tested (60 commits, zero ever delete a line, with a probe control returning 4 positives on pending-pings.jsonl), and the cost stated (two sides appending the same id both survive, which is deliberate). If the reviewer would rather keep the self-land, the alternative is to split `.gitattributes` into its own PR and restore `landing: "self"` here.
why:
TOOLING + TESTS. scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py (a client-side git merge driver — it runs on a session's `git merge`, never on GitHub's servers and never in the trading process), its pytest module, one checklist row, one pipeline row, and the `.gitattributes` mapping described above. No src/, no config, no order path, no account mode, no workflow.

THE CHANGE: `updated_by` was in neither TIMESTAMP_KEYS nor COUPLED_WITH, and both sides of every register conflict always stamp it, so two lanes with provably disjoint row sets still hit Refuse('header scalars disagree and are not bookkeeping timestamps'). It is now resolved as its own kind (AUTHORSHIP_KEYS) by UNIONING both names rather than taking the later one — a union cannot lose a fact, where a pick-a-side rule discards one. The ` + ` separator is the form the E31 lane used resolving this same conflict by hand.

MEASURED, population stated: the 20 adjacent register-touching commit pairs on origin/main dated 2026-09-22, each simulated as base=A^ / ours=A / theirs=B. Driver refusals 5 -> 4; header-only refusals 2 -> 0. Over the 33 pairs since the 2026-09-21 reset: 13 -> 12, header-only 2 -> 0.

⚠️ THE OBVIOUS FIX IS INERT, found by re-measuring after shipping it: COUPLED_WITH = {'updated_at': ('updated_by',)} fires on ZERO real conflicts, because MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json stamps updated_at at DATE granularity, so two lanes landing the same day write it identically and git never marks that line. The coupling alone moved the count 5 -> 5.

THE REFUSAL DID NOT WEAKEN. Pair f50a25928 -> 4ca43ed4a on main disagrees on `updated_by` AND on row R7 and still refuses, on the row. Two planted mutations: the naive fix (later name wins) fails 6 of the new tests; the forbidden 'ignore any scalar you do not recognise' escape fails the PRE-EXISTING test_REFUSE_non_timestamp_header_divergence. tests/ops/test_merge_json_register.py extended 21 -> 32 cases, all green, every pre-existing case unchanged.

OBSERVED TWICE ON THIS BRANCH, not only tested: main moved under the PR twice, and on each armed `git merge` the driver resolved MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json cleanly (zero ids lost from either side, header naming both writers) — the second time while PIPELINE.jsonl conflicted beside it, which is what the .gitattributes line now fixes.
